resources.string: Confirm it is you to open your conversation.
TenChar keeps its keys behind your phone\'s screen lock. Without a PIN, pattern or password it will not run.
Two quick choices before you start. You can change both later in Settings.
A relay passes encrypted messages between your phones. Using a backup relay keeps messages flowing if the main one is down, but a second relay also sees your IP address and timing.
Used if the main relay is down
Make a one-time code on one phone and type it on the other. The code works once and is deleted after pairing.
The numbers did not match. The pairing was cancelled and its keys were deleted. Make a new code to try again.
Conversation forgotten. Pair again to start a new one.
No phone answered with that code. Check the code, and that both phones use the same relays, then try again.
Could not reach a relay. Check your connection and try again.
The relays gave different answers, or the other side\'s keys did not match its commitment. The pairing was cancelled for your safety.
That code has already been used by two phones. Make a new code.
Could not save the keys on this phone. Try again.
That code is not valid. It has 16 letters and numbers.
Type this code on the other phone within 24 hours. Share it only with that person, in person or over a channel you trust.
Checking the code and finding the other phone. The first connection can take up to a minute while a relay wakes up.
Both phones must show the same number. Compare it by voice or in person, not by message through this app. This check is what protects you against a malicious relay.
The message box is full. Send it, then keep writing.
Too long for one message. It will be sent as %1$d messages.
Offline. Messages will send when a relay can be reached.
The relays no longer have this conversation. You may need to pair again.
Could not load. Tap to try again.
Videos can be up to 30 seconds. Trim it in your gallery and try again.

Allow the microphone in system settings to record voice messages.
A quiet background service checks your relays and shows “New message”. No Google or push server is involved.
Many phones need this to keep alerts arriving while the screen is off.
Allow notifications for TenChar in system settings to see alerts.
An alert says only “New message”: never who sent it, which chat, or what it says. The service cannot open your chats, which stay locked.
TenChar asks your relays whether a message is waiting. Tap to open.
Both phones must use the same relay, or they cannot pair. The relay cannot read your messages, but it can see your IP address and when you connect.
Changing these applies to chats you pair from now on. Each chat keeps the relays it was paired on.
Enter an https address such as https://relay.example.com, with no username, path or query.
Messages and keys on this phone are deleted. You will need to pair again. This cannot be undone.

A private end-to-end encrypted messenger. Each chat is between two people, and a message can be up to 500 characters; longer text is sent as several messages. You can also send photos, voice messages and short videos.

Every message is encrypted on your phone with a Double Ratchet, and the relay only ever holds ciphertext. Photos, voice messages and videos are encrypted on your phone with a key of their own before they are uploaded, and photos are stripped of location and camera data. Optional alerts come from a small background service in this app: no Google or third-party push service is involved.

The cryptography is composed by hand from standard primitives (X25519, HKDF, AES-GCM). It is open source but has not been independently reviewed. Do not rely on it where a mistake could put someone in danger.
What TenChar will not protect against
Malware or a compromised OS on an unlocked phone, screen readers, and accessibility services with permission.
A third-party keyboard that records what you type.
Metadata: the relay and Cloudflare can see IP addresses, timing, message counts and sizes. The app does not hide your IP.
The other person keeping, screenshotting or forwarding what you send.
Denial of service, and relay availability.
A weak lock screen on the phone.
Message length: a longer message needs more encrypted pieces, so a relay can see roughly how long each message is.

Attachments and alerts: the relay can see that you sent a photo, voice message or video, when, and roughly how big it was (rounded up to 16 KiB), never what is in it. With alerts on, it can see which chats this phone checks and how often.
